plan.title: Your first 10 minutes
plan.subtitle: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star
plan.intro: A short plan for using this edition. Ten minutes is a focused start, not a promise to learn the whole piece.

steps.title: Get the right edition
steps.body: Open the Early Elementary version named above. Keep the edition title in view so that the score and tutorial match. The provider may ask for your name and email or a sign-in.
steps.helpBody: You can read the plan first. Access to the music is handled by the provider, not by PianoGrid.

steps.title: Find the starting position
steps.body: Use the hand-position graphic and instructions in this edition. Find the starting keys on your own piano before trying the phrase. Follow the edition’s hand instructions rather than a different arrangement of the song.
steps.helpBody: Use the note finder for an unfamiliar key name. Finger numbers describe fingers; they are not octave numbers.

steps.title: Choose one short phrase
steps.body: Choose a short phrase from this score or its matching tutorial. Work on that section at a pace that lets you follow the notes. You do not need to finish the whole song in this session.
steps.helpBody: Choose a smaller section from the same edition. Check the matching tutorial before deciding where to begin or which hand to use.

steps.title: Repeat one small section
steps.body: Repeat the section you chose. Pause at a place that feels uncertain, check the score or tutorial, and try that small part again. Move on when you are ready; the suggested minutes are not a countdown.
steps.helpBody: For this session, one clearer note change or one more comfortable repetition is a useful thing to notice.

steps.title: Choose what to revisit
steps.body: Use the matching tutorial or reference to check your attempt. Choose one focus for next time: finding the notes, following the rhythm, or coordinating the hands. You may also leave this undecided.
steps.helpBody: These are your own notes about the session. PianoGrid has not listened to or graded your playing.

result.title: A small session, a next step
result.body: You reached the end of the plan. Your check-in is not an assessment of your playing.
result.shareBody: The other person gets the plan and edition details—not your check-ins.

shared.label: Shared practice plan
shared.body: Start at the beginning with the same edition. No one else’s check-ins are included.

expired.title: This plan version is unavailable

learnSections.h2: What makes an arrangement a useful starting point?
learnSections.body: Look at the specific edition, not only the song title. Compare the publisher’s level, the sample, the required hand movement and how the materials are supplied. “Easy” is a label to investigate, not a guarantee that every version will fit your current skills.

Choose a section from the exact score or its matching tutorial. Keep the first goal narrow: locate the starting keys, follow one phrase, or revisit a difficult change. You can shorten the session or return to a step at any time.

learnSections.h2: Do I need chords and scales first?
learnSections.body: Not as a blanket requirement for every arrangement. Start with this edition’s instructions. Use a chord or scale reference when the score or tutorial gives you a specific reason to use it.

learnSections.h2: Where do I get the music?
learnSections.body: The edition pages explain the provider and access route. These three publisher editions are not score or audio downloads hosted by PianoGrid.

teacher.title: A small pack for your next lesson
teacher.subtitle: Piano key names · C4–C5
teacher.body: Use a labeled reference, a write-in worksheet and an answer page to practice white-key names. Print all three pages, or just the worksheet.
teacher.scope: White-key names from C4 to C5. Octave numbers identify register, not fingers.
teacher.caveat: A reference worksheet, not a full-size keyboard sticker template.
